title: Precision-Boundary Lightweight Kernel for Streaming KV+Attention Fusion
creator: Asha Patel
description: Streaming decode workloads pay a heavy penalty when precision boundaries force repeated quant->fp casts for attention and KV updates. This ticket implements a lightweight, precision-boundary-aware microkernel that fuses attention score computation with KV-cache updates on INT8/FP8 execution paths to eliminate redundant conversions and reduce memory traffic. The kernel will use head-aware scale compensation and accumulate in a narrow accumulation format to keep latency and memory overhead low while maintaining generation quality. Goals: (1) reduce per-token overhead of precision transition by >= 25% on typical web-scale decodes, (2) keep perplexity/regression within existing SLOs on our regression prompt suite, and (3) integrate with the runtime's scheduling and routing policies so the kernel is selectable as a model-variant fastpath.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end streaming decode for benchmark model (seq_len=64 decode window) shows >=25% reduction in per-token CPU/GPU time spent in cast and staging operations compared to baseline mixed-precision path
No measurable regressions in the prioritized evaluation prompt set: top-1 output quality within 0.5% of baseline or better
Microkernel exposes an opt-in config flag and is selectable by model-variant and routing policy in the runtime catalog
Perf telemetry added: breakdown of time spent in precision boundary bridging, KV writebacks, attention compute; dashboards updated
Automated tests cover correctness against FP32 reference for a representative set of heads and sequences
implementation_plan: Design: finalize API for kernel selector and runtime hinting (2 days)
Prototype: implement kernel in C++/CUDA with zero-copy staging and compensated int8 accumulation (4 days)
Benchmark: microbench harness for per-head streaming decode, compare int8/ffp8 fused path to baseline (2 days)
Integration: wire kernel into kernel registry, add runtime selection policy and config flags (2 days)
Safety: add unit tests, quant/regression evals, and a canary rollout in dedicated pool (3 days)
Rollout: gradual enablement behind feature flag with telemetry gating (release runtime-2026.04)
progress_updates: 2026-03-06: Kickoff meeting with serving runtime and eval teams. Agreed on primary metric: per-token bridge time and KV write latency.
2026-03-08: Spike kernel prototyped in isolated harness. Initial fused path reduces cast copies but has accumulation drift on long sequences; discovered headwise scale mismatches.
2026-03-10: Implemented head-aware scale compensation and int32 accumulation window to remove drift. Microbenchmark shows 28% reduction in cast+staging time for seq=32 decode.
2026-03-12: Added unit tests and small regression suite. Started integration with kernel selector; selector API requires small change to accept 'precision_boundary_hint'.
2026-03-13: Perf dashboards patched to accept new telemetry counters. Preparing canary config for dedicated pool.
blockers: Need GPU driver quirk resolved for int8 warp-level atomics on our smallest Dedicated instance (tic: infra-1164)
Kernel selector API change requires a short runtime rollout window to avoid selector mismatch errors
notes: Trade-offs: the fused path increases code complexity and maintenance surface but the telemetry shows substantial cost/latency wins for streaming inference workloads.
Fallback plan: if accumulation drift persists at long sequence lengths, fall back to a hybrid path that does periodic light-weight fp32 reconciliation every N tokens.
Telemetry plan: emit counters for 'bridge_ms', 'kv_write_ms', 'attn_compute_ms', and headwise scale factors to detect drift in production.
Quality targets: run full eval suite behind a gating job; if any metric outside bounds, automatically disable kernel via rollout policy.
